That instinct checks out. I grepped the codebase — the only place using a real per-component `<Suspense>` boundary is `src/app/footy/info/page.tsx`; everywhere else "loading" just means the single page-level `loading.tsx` Next.js generates automatically. Since your pages fetch data once and pass it down as props (by design, to keep data logic server-side), there's no actual incremental/streaming reveal happening — so a skeleton that mirrors individual components' layout is pure decoration with no functional payoff, and it's the thing drifting out of sync with the real components as you've found.

Given that, I'd go all the way: delete every `*Skeleton.tsx` (and their stories/tests) and the generic `Skeletons` component, and replace every route's `loading.tsx` with the same `Flex` + `Loader type="dots"` pattern your root `src/app/loading.tsx` already uses. One honest "loading" state everywhere, nothing to keep in sync with page layouts. The only real tradeoff is losing the (mostly illusory, given no streaming) perceived-layout-stability skeletons give.

content.text:
Yes — Next.js walks up the segment tree and uses the nearest ancestor `loading.tsx` for anything that doesn't define its own, so root's `app/loading.tsx` already covers every route underneath by default. I checked the layout tree to make sure that's safe here:

- `CustomAppShell` (the nav/chrome) sits in `app/layout.tsx` **around** `{children}` — the part Next.js wraps in the Suspense boundary is only the routed content inside it, so the nav won't flicker or remount during loading, regardless of which `loading.tsx` catches the fallback.
- The nested layouts in between (`footy/layout.tsx`, `footy/(authenticated)/layout.tsx`, `footy/admin/layout.tsx`) don't render persistent visible chrome — just a notification listener and an async auth-role redirect — so having them fall inside the fallback region during navigation is harmless.

So deleting all the per-route `loading.tsx` (and their `.stories.tsx` pairs) and leaning entirely on the root one is safe and removes real duplication, since every one of them was just going to become the same `Flex` + `Loader type="dots"` anyway.

One thing worth flagging for later, not a blocker now: if you ever add a nested layout with actual visible chrome (breadcrumbs, tabs, etc.) sitting below root, that chrome would disappear during the fallback unless that layout gets its own `loading.tsx`. Not the case today.

Want me to go ahead and delete: every `*Skeleton.tsx` (+ stories/tests), the generic `Skeletons` component, and every route's `loading.tsx`/`loading.stories.tsx` except the root one?

# Run the project's mandatory finalisation checklist before reporting any task as done

## Steps

1. Run `npm run typecheck` and capture all output.
2. Run `npm run lint` and capture all output.
3. Run `npx knip` and capture all output.
4. If any of the three produced errors or warnings:
   - For lint issues — run `npm run lint:fix` first to auto-fix what it can, then re-run `npm run lint` to see what remains.
   - For knip findings — remove the unused files, exports, or dependencies it reports.
   - Fix **every** remaining issue — do not skip, suppress, or dismiss any output.
   - If you are unsure whether a problem existed before your changes, run `git stash`, repeat all three commands to establish a pre-change baseline, then `git stash pop` and fix only the new issues.
   - After fixing, re-run all three commands to confirm they are clean.
5. Repeat until all three commands exit with code 0 and report no errors or warnings.

## Done criterion

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npx knip` all exit with code 0 and report no errors or warnings. Only then report the task as complete.

## Notes

- Fix issues in the order they appear — later errors are often caused by earlier ones.
- Avoid silencing a lint rule or adding a `@ts-ignore` / `eslint-disable` comment to make the output go away — fix the underlying problem. If a suppression is truly necessary (false positive, required vendor API), scope it as narrowly as possible (single line, specific rule) and add a short inline comment explaining why.
- If a typecheck error is in a generated file (`prisma/generated/`, `prisma/zod/`), do not edit it — regenerate it with `npx prisma generate` instead.
